title: Finite-group quotient atlas pullbacks are the defining torsors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $H$ be a finite abstract group acting by $S$-automorphisms on an $S$-scheme $Z$, and put $H_T=\coprod_{h\in H}T$ with its constant group law for every $S$-scheme $T$. Define $[Z/H](T)$ to be the groupoid of pairs $(P,v)$, where $P$ is a sheaf on the big fppf site of $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with an $H_T$-action which becomes the translation action on $H_T$ after an fppf covering, and $v:P\to Z$ is equivariant; arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with $v$. Let $q:Z\to[Z/H]$ send $z:T\to Z$ to the trivial torsor with map $(h,t)\mapsto h\cdot z(t)$. For every object $\xi=(P,v)\in[Z/H](T)$, the $2$-fibre product $Z\times_{[Z/H],\xi}T$ is canonically represented by the torsor $P$, which is a finite etale surjective $T$-scheme [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Here the $2$-fibre product has pairs of objects with a specified isomorphism as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its sections over $T$ correspond exactly to pairs $(z,\eta)$ with $z:T\to Z$ and $\eta:q(z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi$; all these identifications commute with base change in $T$. No freeness of the action on $Z$, invertibility of $|H|$, or finite-type hypothesis on $Z$ is assumed.

The finite constant group specialization uses fppf descent of finite etale schemes, not invertibility of the group order.

proof.text: For a test scheme $a:U\to T$, the 2-fibre product has objects $(z,\eta)$ with $z:U\to Z$ and $\eta:q(z)\simeq\xi|_U$. Its arrows over $U$ are identities: the two scheme factors are discrete, and their identity arrows force equality of $\eta$. Send $(z,\eta)$ to $p=\eta(1)\in P(U)$. Equivariance forces $\eta(h)=h\cdot p$ as a map of sheaves, and compatibility with $v$ gives $z=v(p)$. This uses the fibrewise 2-product definition of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 0371 (remark-X-mod-G-group), explicit trivial torsor functor of Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks)

proof.text: Conversely, given $p\in P(U)$, set $z=v(p)$ and $\eta_p(h)=h\cdot p$. Then $v(\eta_p(h))=h\cdot z$, so it commutes with the maps to $Z$. It is an isomorphism: on a covering trivializing $P$, write $p=k$ in $H_U$; the map is right multiplication by $k$, with inverse right multiplication by $k^{-1}$. These inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same map, and hence glue by the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Evaluation at $1$ and this construction are mutually inverse, since every equivariant map out of $H_U$ has $\eta(h)=h\eta(1)$.

source.place: Tag 0371 (remark-X-mod-G-group), torsor description and Tag 04WM trivial-object functor

proof.text: Choose an fppf trivializing cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ of $P$. Locally the representing scheme is $X_i=\coprod_{h\in H}T_i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. It is finite: over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}(A^H)$, and the finitely many coordinate vectors generate $A^H$ as an $A$-module, exactly the finite-morphism definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Each summand maps by the identity, which is etale from its definition, so [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale] gives etaleness.

source.place: Tag 0BLZ (lemma-finite-etale-stack), input finite etale local schemes; finite constant-group specialization

proof.text: The sheaf $P$ with its local representations $X_i$ gives overlap scheme isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle by [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-fppf-descent] to obtain a finite etale $T$-scheme $X$ inducing that datum. The representability/effectivity assertion of [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] then identifies $h_X$ with the original sheaf $P$, inducing the chosen local trivializations. With Steps 1–2 this represents the 2-fibre product; its map to $Z$ is $v$.

The map $X\to T$ is surjective: for $t\in T$, choose $t_i\in T_i$ above it using joint surjectivity of the trivializing fppf cover [def-pc-fppf-site]; the identity summand of $X\times_TT_i\simeq H_{T_i}$ supplies a point of $X$ above $t$. For $b:U'\to U$, restriction sends $\eta(1)$ to $(b^*\eta)(1)$ and sends $h\cdot p$ to $h\cdot b^*p$. Thus both inverse identifications commute with every base change and their composites. Representability and the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identify the pulled-back representing scheme with $X\times_TT'$. At $U=T$ the same bijection gives precisely the asserted sections. The argument uses neither freeness on $Z$ nor division by $|H|$ nor finite type of $Z$.
